blocks.text:
What to notice:

- `getInputStream()` is the child's **standard output** as seen by the parent (the naming is from the parent's point of view). `redirectErrorStream(true)` merges stderr into it, which is why `err` appears in the stream.
- **Read the output.** If the child writes more than the operating system's pipe buffer holds and nobody reads, the child blocks and `waitFor()` hangs forever. Either consume the stream (as above), merge stderr, or redirect output to a file with `redirectOutput(File)`, or to the parent's console with `inheritIO()`.
- `waitFor()` returns the exit code; `waitFor(timeout, unit)` returns `false` on timeout, after which you decide: `destroy()` (polite, SIGTERM) or `destroyForcibly()` (SIGKILL).
- `directory(File)` sets the working directory and `environment()` is a mutable copy of the environment for the child only.
- `ProcessHandle` (Java 9) exposes pids, parent and children, and `onExit()` returns a `CompletableFuture`.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Command injection. Never build a command by concatenating user input into a string passed to `sh -c`: `"ls " +` `userInput` with `; rm -rf ~` as input runs both. Pass user data as a separate argument element (`new` `ProcessBuilder("ls", userInput)`), which reaches the program without shell interpretation, and validate it anyway (a value beginning with `-` can still be read as an option by the program).

blocks.title: Interview angle
blocks.text: How do you run code when a Java application is stopped, and when does it not run? Register a shutdown hook with `Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook(thread)`. The JVM runs it on normal exit, `System.exit`, and on SIGTERM or Ctrl+C. It does not run on `kill -9`, `Runtime.halt`, power loss or a JVM crash, so critical data must not depend on it. Hooks run concurrently, so keep them independent and quick.

blocks.title: Real world
blocks.text: In containers, the platform sends SIGTERM, waits for a grace period and then SIGKILL. A Spring Boot service with graceful shutdown enabled (`server.shutdown=graceful`) stops accepting new requests, finishes in-flight ones, and closes pools from the shutdown hook; a service that ignores this drops requests on each deployment.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
The process context (arguments, properties, environment, exit code) is how a Java program is configured and observed from outside.

- `-Dkey=value` before the class sets system properties; `System.getenv` reads environment variables; both return `null` when missing.
- `Properties` loads `key=value` text; byte streams mean ISO-8859-1, so pass a UTF-8 `Reader` for modern files.
- Shutdown hooks run on exit, `System.exit` and SIGTERM/SIGINT, never on `kill -9` or `halt`; keep them short and independent.
- Exit code 0 is success; an uncaught exception gives 1; call `System.exit` only at the outermost layer.
- With `ProcessBuilder` pass arguments separately, drain the child's output, use timeouts, and never concatenate user input into a shell string.
#### Exceptions

items.question: What does this print: `static int m() { try { throw new RuntimeException(); } catch (Exception e) {` `return 1; } finally { System.out.print("F "); } }` followed by `System.out.println(m());`?
items.answer: `F 1`. The `catch` chooses the return value `1`, `finally` prints `F` before the method actually returns, and the caller prints `1`.

items.question: What is wrong with `catch (Exception e) { ... } catch (IOException e) { ... }` in that order?
items.answer: It does not compile: the second clause is unreachable because `Exception` already catches every `IOException`. Put the specific type first.

items.question: Which of these are checked: `IOException`, `IllegalStateException`, `OutOfMemoryError`, `InterruptedException`?
items.answer: `IOException` and `InterruptedException` are checked. `IllegalStateException` is unchecked (a `RuntimeException`) and `OutOfMemoryError` is an `Error`, so also unchecked.

items.question: What does this print: `StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("a"); try { return` `sb.append("b").toString(); } finally { sb.append("c"); }` (the method returns the String)?
items.answer: The method returns `ab`. The `String` was produced before `finally` ran, and appending `c` to the builder afterwards does not change it (the program prints `ab`).

items.question: A try-with-resources body throws A and closing the resource throws B. Which exception does the caller see, and where is the other one?
items.answer: The caller sees A (the primary exception). B is attached to A and is available from `A.getSuppressed()`.

items.question: Why does `assert list.remove(x);` count as a bug?
items.answer: Assertions are disabled by default, so the `remove` would never run in a normal run. Assertions must have no side effects.

blocks.text: #### Logging and debugging basics

items.question: A logger is set to `INFO`. Which of these appear: `fine`, `info`, `warning`, `severe`?
items.answer: `info`, `warning` and `severe`. `fine` is below the threshold and is discarded.

items.question: Why is `log.debug("user=" + user)` worse than `log.debug("user={}", user)`?
items.answer: The first builds the concatenated string (and calls `user.toString()`) every time, even when debug is disabled. The second does the work only if the level is enabled.

items.question: What is wrong with this catch block? `catch (IOException e) { log.error(e.getMessage()); }`
items.answer: It logs only the message, not the exception object, so the stack trace and the cause chain are lost. Use `log.error("...", e)`.

items.question: In JUL, what happens if the logger allows `FINE` but the `ConsoleHandler` is at its default level?
items.answer: The record is dropped by the handler. A record must pass the logger level and the handler level; the default `ConsoleHandler` level is `INFO`, so `FINE` messages do not appear until you set the handler to `FINE` or `ALL`.

items.question: What does a conditional breakpoint save you from?
items.answer: Pausing and resuming manually on every iteration or call; it stops only when the condition (for example a particular id) is true.

blocks.text: #### Classic I/O

items.question: What does `InputStream.read()` return at the end of the stream, and why is its return type `int`?
items.answer: It returns `-1`. The type is `int` so that all 256 byte values (0 to 255) can be distinguished from the end marker; a `byte` could not represent -1 as "end" without clashing with the valid byte 0xFF.

items.question: In `new BufferedReader(new FileReader(f))`, which object do you close, and what happens to the other?
items.answer: Close only the outer `BufferedReader` (the try-with-resources variable). Closing it closes the wrapped `FileReader` and the file.

items.question: What is wrong with this snippet? `PrintWriter pw = new PrintWriter("out.txt"); pw.println("hi");` (no close).
items.answer: Without `close()` or `flush()` the data may stay in the buffer and never reach the file; and the file handle leaks. Use try-with-resources.

items.question: A file written by `new FileWriter(f, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)` is read with ISO-8859-1. The text contains the single character `é`. What do you see?
items.answer: Two characters, shown as "Ã©", because UTF-8 stored the character as the two bytes C3 A9 and ISO-8859-1 maps each byte to its own character (mojibake).

items.question: `Scanner sc` reads `42\nAsha\n` with `int n = sc.nextInt(); String s = sc.nextLine();`. What is `s`?
items.answer: The empty string `""`: `nextInt()` consumed `42` but left the newline, and `nextLine()` returned the rest of that first line.

items.question: Why does `copyBlock` in the listing beat the buffered byte-by-byte copy?
items.answer: It makes one method call and one system call per 8 KiB instead of one method call per byte, so there is far less overhead, even though both avoid a system call per byte.

blocks.text: #### NIO.2: Paths, Files and Channels

items.question: What is `Path.of("/a/b").resolve("/c")`, and why does it matter for security?
items.answer: It is `/c`: resolving an absolute path replaces the base. Untrusted names must be normalized and checked with `startsWith(base)`, or an attacker can escape the intended directory.

items.question: What is wrong with `Files.lines(p).forEach(System.out::println);` in a long-running application?
items.answer: The stream holds an open file handle and is never closed. Use try-with-resources: `try (Stream<String> s =` `Files.lines(p)) { ... }`.

items.question: A `ByteBuffer` has just been filled by `put` calls. What must you do before writing it to a channel, and what does that call change?
items.answer: Call `flip()`: it sets the limit to the current position and the position to 0, so the channel reads exactly the bytes you wrote.

items.question: `Files.move(a, b)` where `b` already exists: what happens?
items.answer: It throws `FileAlreadyExistsException`; pass `StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING` to overwrite.

items.question: Does `HttpClient.send` throw for an HTTP 500 response?
items.answer: No. It returns a response whose `statusCode()` is 500. Only I/O problems (connection refused, timeout) throw.

items.question: Why is `normalize()` unreliable when a path contains symbolic links?
items.answer: `normalize()` only edits the text of the path. `a/link/../b` where `link` points elsewhere means a different place on disk than `a/b`, which only `toRealPath()` (it consults the file system) resolves correctly.

blocks.text: #### Serialization and Its Dangers

items.question: What does this print, assuming `class P implements Serializable { transient int n = 5; int m = 7; }` is written and read back after `n` and `m` were both changed to 9 before writing?
items.answer: `n` is `0` (transient fields get default values) and `m` is `9`.

items.question: Is the constructor of a `Serializable` class called when an object is deserialized? What about its non-serializable superclass?
items.answer: No, the constructor of the serializable class is not called. The no-arg constructor of the first non-serializable superclass is called, and that superclass's fields are not restored from the stream.

items.question: Why should you declare `serialVersionUID` explicitly?
items.answer: The computed default changes whenever the class changes, even for compatible edits, breaking old data. A declared value lets you decide when compatibility ends.

items.question: A class is `Serializable` and has a field `private Thread worker;`. What happens on `writeObject`, and what are two fixes?
items.answer: `NotSerializableException: java.lang.Thread`. Mark the field `transient` (and recreate it lazily or in `readObject`), or do not keep the thread in the object.

items.question: Explain how deserializing untrusted bytes can run attacker-chosen code even though your program only calls `readObject` and casts to `Account`.
items.answer: `readObject` creates the object graph the stream describes before your cast; classes on the class path with dangerous `readObject` or `hashCode` logic (gadgets) run while the stream is read, so the cast failing afterwards is too late.

items.question: Name two safer alternatives and one JDK mechanism that limits the damage when you cannot avoid `ObjectInputStream`.
items.answer: JSON (Jackson) or Protobuf into known types; an `ObjectInputFilter` allow-list (per stream or `jdk.serialFilter`) with depth and size limits.

blocks.text: #### Properties, System and Runtime

items.question: What is printed by `java -Dflag=true Main` for `System.out.println(Boolean.getBoolean("flag") + " " +` `Boolean.getBoolean("true"));`?
items.answer: `true false`. `Boolean.getBoolean(name)` looks up a system property named `name`; no property called `true` exists.

items.question: A shutdown hook closes a database pool. In which of these situations does it run: `System.exit(1)`, Ctrl+C, `kill -9`, uncaught exception in `main`?
items.answer: It runs for `System.exit(1)`, Ctrl+C (SIGINT) and the uncaught exception in `main` (once the other non-daemon threads finish and the JVM exits normally). It does not run for `kill -9`.

items.question: What is wrong with this: `Process p = new ProcessBuilder("producer").start(); p.waitFor();` when `producer` prints several megabytes?
items.answer: The child blocks when the pipe buffer fills because the parent never reads it, so `waitFor()` hangs. Read the stream, merge or redirect stderr, redirect output to a file, or use `inheritIO()`.

items.question: Why is `new ProcessBuilder("sh", "-c", "grep " + term + " log.txt")` dangerous, and what is the safer form?
items.answer: The term is interpreted by the shell, so `x; rm -rf ~` runs a second command. Use `new ProcessBuilder("grep",` `"--", term, "log.txt")`, with no shell, and validate the term.

items.question: Which charset does `Properties.load(InputStream)` use, and how do you read a UTF-8 properties file correctly?
items.answer: ISO-8859-1, with `\uXXXX` escapes for other characters. Wrap the stream in an `InputStreamReader` with `StandardCharsets.UTF_8` and call `load(Reader)`.

items.question: What is the exit status of a JVM whose `main` throws an uncaught exception?
items.answer: 1, after the stack trace is printed.
